notes: C4 has no primary structural asset because the command is carried through a bus record field and FIFO data signals, all of which are barred as primaries by the stated rules.
C6 and C7 use bus_rsp_o.data as a carrier only because a bus response record field cannot be primary.
The FIFO instances are black boxes; FIFO data-path observations and influences use the specified one-instance black-box assumption.

points.reason: A bus write changes ctrl.enable, and its value clears both FIFOs, resets timing and controls serial operation.

points.reached by: the bus_access arrow reaches clkgen_en_o with ctrl.enable
points.reason: The output directly carries ctrl.enable, so changing or suppressing it changes the exported enable and can disable the external clock function.
Bus writes set the prescaler and divider, which control whether and when clk_tick is generated.

points.reached by: the bus_access arrow reaches clock_generator with ctrl.clk_prsc, ctrl.clk_div and ctrl.enable
points.reason: This block uses the settings during normal timing generation but does not expose or independently modify the stored configuration.

points.reached by: the clock_generator arrow reaches serial_engine with clk_tick and clk_tick2
points.reason: The timing pulses pace serial steps, but this block does not independently expose or modify the timing configuration.
A bus write changes ctrl.clear, and the clear-derived FIFO inputs can clear both transmit and receive buffers.

points.reached by: the bus_access arrow reaches fifo.rx_clr with ctrl.clear and ctrl.enable
points.reason: This wire only implements the normal clear control path and does not independently expose or modify the stored clear setting.

points.reached by: the bus_access arrow reaches fifo.tx_clr with ctrl.clear and ctrl.enable
points.reason: This wire only implements the normal clear control path and does not independently expose or modify the stored clear setting.
The FIFO clear input is the designed use of the setting; no separate unauthorized mechanism is shown at this black-box boundary.
The FIFO clear input is the designed use of the setting; no separate unauthorized mechanism is shown at this black-box boundary.
Bus data is accepted into the transmit FIFO, so an injected command can alter the selected operation or occupy the engine.

points.reached by: the bus_req_i arrow reaches fifo.tx_wdata with bus_req_i.data
points.reason: The transmit command and byte are formed directly from bus request data before entering the FIFO.
By the black-box FIFO rule, the value entering its write-data port can affect its later read-data output.
The command field selects the bit, byte or reset state, and a reset command keeps the engine in its reset sequence.
The bus write supplies the transmitted byte and command to the transmit FIFO.

points.reached by: the bus_req_i arrow reaches fifo.tx_wdata with bus_req_i.data
points.reason: The FIFO write-data signal is formed from the bus byte field and can therefore carry a changed byte.
By the black-box FIFO rule, the written byte can be returned on the FIFO read-data port.
The FIFO byte is loaded into serial.sreg and its bits influence the one-wire drive decisions.

points.reached by: holding block and the onewire_i arrow reaches serial_engine
points.reason: The external one-wire input is sampled into wire_in and used to form the received byte and presence result.

points.reached by: serial_engine reaches fifo.rx_wdata with serial.presence and serial.sreg
points.reason: This wire only carries the assembled receive word into the receive FIFO.
By the black-box FIFO rule, the received word entering the FIFO can later appear at its read-data output.
A bus read returns the receive byte and presence bit, while request fields select whether that received result is returned.

points.reached by: holding block and the onewire_i arrow reaches serial_engine
points.reason: The synchronized one-wire level is sampled into serial.wire_in and later used for the sense read-back.

points.reached by: the serial_engine arrow reaches bus_access with serial.wire_in
points.reason: The sense bit is returned only for the selected read, so request address, direction and strobe can control whether software receives that level.
The interrupt output is assigned from enable, transmit-FIFO availability and serial busy state, so changing any operand can create or suppress the request.

points.reached by: the tx_fifo_inst arrow reaches irq_generator with fifo.tx_avail
points.reason: By the black-box rule, the FIFO availability output can affect the interrupt expression and therefore whether service is requested.
The busy state is an operand of the interrupt equation, and its state-derived value can suppress the interrupt.

points.reached by: the bus_access arrow reaches irq_generator with ctrl.enable
points.reason: A bus write changes the enable operand that the interrupt generator requires before asserting irq_o.
